response:
It sounds like you're in a really painful spot—holding onto hope while also knowing he hasn't shown genuine interest in more. That mixed signaling, especially the physical closeness, makes it much harder to move on because it keeps feeding those fantasies.

Honestly, maintaining the friendship as it currently exists may not be realistic right now. His casual touching and attention are giving you false hope, even if he doesn't intend it that way. To get him out of your system, you likely need real distance—not just a different office, but boundaries on conversation frequency and physical contact. You can be kind but honest: something like, "I value our friendship, but I need some space to reset." A true friend will respect that. Also, be gentle with yourself—three years of connection and attraction don't disappear quickly. Consider redirecting that emotional energy toward people and activities that nourish you outside of this dynamic. If the friendship is meant to survive, it can withstand a period of distance while you heal.
